turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_fatigue_train.csv: 293 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT, TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si,
    Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and `target` (the
    measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).
  - b3_fatigue_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose rotating-bending
    fatigue strength (MPa) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the
    same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST rotating-
bending fatigue strength (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from the
pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
# Analysis

Looking at the training data, the clearest pattern is that fatigue strength is dominated by the **process route**, not just composition. The NT=930 samples (through-hardened, oil-quenched alloy steels with Cr/Mo additions, tempered at low temperatures of 160–200°C) show dramatically higher fatigue strength (900–1144 MPa) than any other process group in the dataset (case-hardened NT=825–900 series max out around 400–650 MPa; even the high-Si NT=845 series only reaches ~700–900 MPa).

Within the NT=930 group, the highest training values occur with:
- Tempering temperature (TT) = 160°C (200°C consistently costs ~40–65 MPa vs. 160°C, based on matched-composition pairs)
- Moderate-to-high Cr (0.6–1.2%) and Mo (0.15–0.2%) content
- RedRatio around 440–690
- Longer carburizing/quench times (Ct) tend to slightly increase strength for matched compositions

I matched each NT=930 pool candidate to its nearest composition/process twin(s) in the training set:

- **c081**: Nearly identical composition/process to the single highest training sample (1144 MPa, C=0.21, Cr=1.17, Mo=0.17, RedRatio=690, TT=160), differing only by TT=200. Estimated ~1090 MPa — the strongest candidate.
- **c063**: Matches a training twin (Ct=139.8, TT=160, same comp) at 1034 MPa; longer Ct (469.8) trend suggests slightly higher, ~1040–1050 MPa.
- **c016**: Matches training twin exactly at TT=160 (1082 MPa); TT=200 penalty brings it to an estimated ~1020–1040 MPa.
- **c046**: Exact match to a training row → 1033 MPa.
- **c000**: Twin composition (QmT=60,Ct=340.2,TT=160) scores 1028 MPa in training; QmT=140 causes a small, inconsistent shift, so estimated ~1000–1020 MPa.

Other NT=930 candidates (c018, c054, c050, c053, c062, c075) match twins scoring 927–1009 MPa — all outside the top 5.

# Final Ranking

Final: c081, c063, c016, c046, c000
